facts.claim: Under the Storting's law on visitor contributions (decision of 5 June 2025), a municipality may charge an overnight fee of 3% of the payment for the stay excluding VAT (§ 2-3); it applies to the whole municipality (§ 2-1), to stays of under 30 consecutive days, the duty arises when the stay begins, the fee must be itemised in sales documents, and the municipality may set which months it applies; the ministry must approve the municipality's plan before the fee takes effect (§ 2-2).

It applies to stays of under 30 consecutive days
The duty to pay arises when the stay begins

facts.claim: Tromsø's council (kommunestyret) decided on 24 June 2026 to introduce the overnight fee, planned from 1 January 2027; the plan must be approved by the ministry before the fee can take effect (no approval found as of 28 Oct 2026); the draft local regulation is on public consultation with responses due 30 October 2026; the consultation does not cover the rate, which the city says is set in the law at 3%.

facts.claim: Visit Tromsø says the polar night lasts approximately from 27 November to 15 January, with a few hours of twilight a day; light returns gradually from mid-January and the sun is usually not visible from central Tromsø until later in January because of the surrounding mountains.

facts.claim: Visit Tromsø says the northern lights may be visible from late August to early April, that clear skies and darkness are essential, and that Tromsø lies within the auroral zone; it makes no guarantee of sightings.
